answer: Sybil resistance can come from slashable identity bonds paired with quadratic voting. From the dawn of registration, every agent locks a bond and receives voting weight equal to the square root of its stake, so influence rises sublinearly throughout an agent's voyage. Peers audit attestations and slash any wallet caught farming an oasis of clones. Doubling a vote therefore costs roughly four times the locked capital, and each forged identity risks losing its entire bond, so attacking costs far more than cooperating.
